# requireSafeInteger

<link-summary>Returns the value as a safe integer, or throws.</link-summary>

<web-summary>requireSafeInteger() — Returns the value as a safe integer, or throws. apps-script-utils, English.</web-summary>

<tldr>
<p>Module: <code>lang/number</code> · Since: 1.11.0</p>
</tldr>

```typescript
function requireSafeInteger(value: unknown, message: string = "Expected a safe integer."): number;
```

An integer that an IEEE-754 double represents exactly. Beyond that range distinct mathematical integers collapse onto the same value and arithmetic quietly stops being exact.

`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).

## Parameters

| Parameter                                             | Type      | Description                                                   |
| :---------------------------------------------------- | :-------- | :------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `value`                                               | `unknown` | The value to validate.                                        |
| `message` _(optional)_ `= "Expected a safe integer."` | `string`  | The message of the exception. A default is used when omitted. |

## Returns

`number` — the same value, typed as a safe integer.

## Throws

| Exception                  | Condition                        |
| :------------------------- | :------------------------------- |
| `IllegalArgumentException` | the value is not a safe integer. |

## Examples

### What passes and what does not

```javascript
requireSafeInteger(42); // => 42
requireSafeInteger(Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER); // => Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER
requireSafeInteger(Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER + 2); // throws IllegalArgumentException
requireSafeInteger(1.5); // throws IllegalArgumentException
```
